subject: china-studies
title: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades

slides.heading: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades
bullets: How one Chinese city becomes urban across the decades: factories and the first housing blocks are built on farmland at the edge as people move in for jobs, the built-up districts spread outward stage by stage, and the urban share climbs 15 to 38 to 62 to 85 while the rural share falls at every stage
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one Chinese city across the decades, watching the farmland at its edge being built over stage by stage as people move in.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain urbanisation as a gradual process driven by people moving in: what is built at each stage and why the urban share climbs at every stage
Read the urban and rural shares at each stage: urban 15, 38, 62, then 85 of every 100 people, with the rural share falling 85, 62, 38, then 15
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to explain why the city grew in stages, not in one leap, and read both shares at every stage.

slides.heading: Two photographs, decades apart - did the city change in one leap?
bullets: Photographs of the same city decades apart look completely different: farmland in one, a built-up city in the other
But a difference between two photographs is not a single step: the change between them happened stage by stage
slides.notes: Ask the class: if the first and last photographs look so different, did the change happen all at once? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation replays every stage in between.

slides.heading: Urbanisation is gradual and driven by people moving in
bullets: Each stage is driven by people moving in: factories offer jobs, migrants arrive, and housing is built for them on farmland at the edge
The built-up area spreads outward stage by stage, and the urban share climbs - and the rural share falls - at every stage
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: people move first for jobs, building follows them, and the shares move a stage at a time - never in one leap.

slides.heading: Stage 1: farmland and a small town
bullets: The map is mostly farmland and a small town stands where the roads cross
Only 15 of every 100 people live in the town: the urban share is 15 and the rural share is 85
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the farmland, the small town and the two share bars: this is the starting point every later stage builds on.

slides.heading: Stage 2: factories and first housing appear
bullets: Factories are built on farmland at the town edge, and their jobs pull people in from the countryside
The first housing blocks rise beside the factories and the urban share climbs to 38 of every 100 people
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the order: factories first, then the people who come for the jobs, then the housing built for them.

slides.heading: Stage 3: built-up districts spread outward
bullets: The built-up districts spread outward from the core and the factories, and the farmland shrinks to a strip in the west
Most people now live in the city: the urban share reaches 62 of every 100 people and the rural share falls to 38
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and point to the farmland strip: the city grows by spreading outward from what is already built, one stage at a time.

slides.heading: Stage 4: a mostly built-up city, reached in stages
bullets: The city is now mostly built-up: 85 of every 100 people live in urban districts and only a small farmland remnant is left
The sudden-leap version is played and corrected: replaying the stages shows the built-up area growing step by step
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and contrast the two versions: the leap replaces everything at once, the replay shows factories, housing and districts arriving stage by stage.

slides.heading: Worked example: reading the shares stage by stage
bullets: Urban share: 15 (s1) to 38 (s2) to 62 (s3) to 85 (s4) of every 100 people - it climbs at every stage and never jumps straight to 85
Rural share: 85 to 62 to 38 to 15 - at each stage the two shares add to 100, so every climb in the urban share is the same fall in the rural share
slides.notes: Work it slowly: read both bars at each stage and check the pair adds to 100. At each step ask: what was built at this stage, and who moved in?

slides.heading: Your turn: explain the next stage
bullets: In pairs: a neighbouring town is at stage 2, with an urban share of 38 - describe what gets built next, who moves in, and what happens to both shares at stage 3
Then swap and check: did your partner grow the city stage by stage from the edge, or slip back to a sudden leap?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for factories and housing spreading outward, the urban share climbing towards 62 and the rural share falling, then take two pairs answers.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says a Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap
Name what is built at each stage and how both shares move to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers walk through the stages in order and read both shares at each one.
